e. Available Housing
Statistics for relocation resources within the City of Richmond attest to the fact that a one-for-one replacement of units of correct sizes and price ranges has been demonstrated for the Randolph Project. Calculation of relocation resources necessarily takes into account relocation that is required for all displacing action programs on a city-wide basis. Total displacement for all such projects that are expected to occur in the City between October 1972 and October 1974, is estimated as 630 families and individuals. New housing unit resources that will become available during that same period and the corresponding need are displayed in the tables below. With a few exceptions (five-bedroom low priced rental units and sales units), adequate resources are available for all projects.

These detailed displacement and resource figures cover only the first two years of a proposed seven year displacement period. In the opinion of HUD relocation specialists, it would be impossible for the applicant to forecast a one-for-one replacement for the remainder of the project. However HUD believes the Authority's generalized staging plans for the whole project sufficiently demonstrate the possibility of satisfactorily completing the project.
